messages.body_plain:
Hi Jim,

The .RData file is saved when you exit R. R usually asks if you want to save the workspace, on exiting. I would recommend always answering No. If you answer Yes, then the whole workspace, including Rattle, is saved to the .RData file.

When you startup R again, it loads up this workspace, hence you get Rattle being loaded also.

I would simply remove (or rename) the .RData file.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject_clean: [SOLVED] Re: help with installing/running Rattle on Mac:
messages.body_plain:
Thanks to David Winsemius for assistance in debugging this and Chris
and Illya for further information. The problem will be fixed in Rattle
version 2.6.11 (not yet released).

The issue is that version 2.6.10 of rattle includes a rattle.ui that
claims to require gtk+ 2.20. The third line of rattle.ui contains:

 <requires lib="gtk+" version="2.20"/>

A simple solution while we wait for a new version of rattle is to
manually edit this file to change the 2.20 to 2.16. There appears no
real dependency on 2.20, and 2.18 seems to work just fine.

So, if you can change this line in the installed package then all
should be okay:

 <requires lib="gtk+" version="2.16"/>

(By default this folder may be hidden but should be located in
/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.13/Resources/library/rattle/etc/rattle.ui.)

Then the next invocation of rattle() should work.

Regards,
Graham
